stages.title: Concept and audience
stages.description: Decide what the book is about, who reads it and what they get from it.
tasks: Write the premise in three sentences
Describe the ideal reader
Find 3 comparable books and note what yours does differently
Set the target length and writing schedule

stages.title: Outline and structure
stages.description: A chapter-by-chapter map you can write against.
tasks: List the main parts and chapters
Write a one-paragraph summary per chapter
Check the order for gaps and repetition
Settle the tone and point of view

stages.title: Research and sources
stages.description: Collect the facts, quotes and references the chapters rely on.
tasks: Gather key sources per chapter
Verify facts, names and dates
Request permissions for quotes where needed
Keep a notes file linked to chapters

stages.title: First draft
stages.description: Get the whole story down without polishing.
tasks: Write chapters 1 to 3
Write the middle chapters
Write the final chapters
Reach the end without editing as you go

stages.title: Structural revision
stages.description: Fix the shape of the book: order, pacing, missing and weak chapters.
tasks: Read the whole draft in one go
Cut or merge weak chapters
Rewrite the opening and ending
Collect feedback from 2-3 beta readers
Apply the feedback that matters

stages.title: Line editing and proofreading
stages.description: Sentence-level polish and a clean text.
tasks: Line edit for clarity and rhythm
Check consistency of names and terms
Proofread for typos and punctuation
Final read-aloud pass

stages.title: Cover and layout
stages.description: How the book looks and is built as a file.
tasks: Brief and choose the cover design
Typeset the interior
Write the blurb and author bio
Prepare ISBN and metadata
Export print and e-book files

stages.title: Publish
stages.description: The book is out and readers can find it.
tasks: Upload files to the publishing platform
Order and check a proof copy
Set price and release date
Announce to friends, readers and communities
